text:
Predicates:
GetsMonkeypox(x) ::: x gets Monkeypox.
MonkeypoxVirus(x) ::: x is a Monkeypox virus.
OccursIn(x, y) ::: x occurs in y.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Mammal(x) ::: x is a mammal.
Human(x) ::: x is a human.
Symptoms(x, y) ::: y is a symptom of x.
FeelsTired(x) ::: x feels tired.
GetFlu(x) ::: x gets the flu.
Premises:
∀x (MonkeypoxVirus(x) ∧ OccursIn(x, y) → GetsMonkeypox(y)) ::: When the Monkeypox virus occurs in a being, it may get Monkeypox.
∀x (MonkeypoxVirus(x) → OccursIn(x, animal)) ::: Monkeypox virus can occur in certain animals.
Human(x) → Mammal(x) ::: Humans are mammals.
Mammal(x) → Animal(x) ::: Mammals are animals.
Symptoms(Monkeypox, fever) ∧ Symptoms(Monkeypox, headache) ∧ Symptoms(Monkeypox, musclePains) ∧ Symptoms(Monkeypox, tiredness) ::: Symptoms of Monkeypox include fever, headache, muscle pains, and tiredness.
FeelingTired(x) → GetFlu(x) ::: People feel tired when they get the flu.
Conclusion:
¬∃x (GetFlu(x)) ::: No one gets the flu.
